name: DS3231 precision real-time clock
description: Maxim DS3231 I2C real-time clock with its temperature-compensated crystal: time and date in BCD with 12/24-hour modes and the century, two alarms driving INT#, a square-wave and a 32 kHz output, the die temperature, the aging offset, and the oscillator-stop flag set at power-up.

pins.name: 32KHZ
pins.doc: 32.768 kHz output, open drain (needs a pull-up)

pins.name: INT_SQW
pins.doc: Alarm interrupt (active low) or square wave, open drain

pins.name: RST
pins.doc: Reset output, active low, open drain: low for 250 ms after power-up

drift_ppm.doc: The crystal's rate off true, ppm (the datasheet holds +-2 ppm from 0 to 40 C)

start.doc: Date and time at power-up, YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS: the power-on 00:00:00 01/01/00, or the time a clock kept by its battery shows

functional.claims: I2C at 0x68 with user buffers synchronised at each START; BCD time and date with 12/24-hour modes, the century bit and a user day of the week; the countdown chain reset by a seconds write; the rate off by drift_ppm and the aging offset; both alarms with every mask combination setting A1F/A2F and pulling INT# with INTCN; the square wave and 32 kHz outputs (open drain) while wired; temperature at power-up, every 64 s or on CONV (BSY, 125 ms), 0.25 C steps; power-on to 2000-01-01 (or the start a battery kept) with OSF and EN32kHz set and RST low 250 ms; no answer below 2.3 V. Matched bit for bit to a real part's ACKs, time and temperature reads (sigrok's captures).
omissions: the battery (VBAT) switchover and timekeeping on battery (EOSC, BBSQW and OSF on power loss have no effect on VCC)
the RST pushbutton input and its debounce
the TCXO's frequency against temperature (the drift is a parameter)
the 1 Hz square wave's phase against the seconds
